name: Sovereign citizen movement
summary: Sovereign citizens hold that the government is an illegitimate product of a conspiracy that replaced the original common-law order with commercial or admiralty law, and that a person can withdraw from it by filings and declarations, after which its laws, taxes and courts have no authority over them. The movement has no founding text or central leadership, grew from the Posse Comitatus and tax protest, and its sources record almost nothing on questions outside law, jurisdiction and consent.
scope: The sovereign citizen movement of the United States and the pseudolegal belief system it shares across countries, as defined by Britannica, the ADL and the SPLC (s1-s3) and by Sarteschi's review (s4): illegitimacy of the government and the strawman, contract and common-law theories. It excludes offshoots such as the Reichsbürger, Moorish groups' own doctrines and the white-supremacist Posse Comitatus, whose positions are other subjects. Because the movement has no canonical text, only tenets the defining sources attribute to it answer.

sources.author: Anti-Defamation League

sources.title: Sovereign Citizens: A Narrative Review with Implications of Violence Towards Law Enforcement (Aggression and Violent Behavior 60, 2021)
sources.author: Christine M. Sarteschi
sources.usedFor: Scholarly definition: the core belief is the illegitimacy of the US government and consequent immunity from its laws; the movement is not ideologically pure.
